findings: Test000..003 are source atlases, not four missing full-screen backgrounds.
Test004/006/007 are base terrain images. Their final background hashes normally change after *.t decorations. Direct raw hash absence is not a complete coverage audit.
Test005 is used without decorations by Guardian via082960->0832f2. cbc31cbf has HD in this manifest.
Every terrain selects eight original *.t layouts, or the exact scene file stored at08fb52 when08fb4e==2.
Tile group03 selects terrain atlas; other nonFE/nonFF groups select common atlas001. Original mask blitter uses five-plane nonzero coverage.
Combat palette starts from the last PIV palette, then original monster/player/terrain functions replace indices. Guardian uses its own9..31 source words and skips terrain replacement.
World map Test008 has a source-bound scene route, so its dynamic marker hash alone is not a coverage count.
bg1a.PIV/bg1c.PIV are intro scrolling tile banks handled by the scroll scene contract, not additional full-screen static backgrounds.
limitations: No freehand tile composition is asserted. The original blitter clips negative Y as -y-1, clamps negative X without source advance and can write across the right edge. Optional runtime exports execute that original code.
Historical combat backgrounds can include original runtime modifications. A missing dynamic hash is an observed lookup hole, not automatically a distinct new image job.
The optional32 layout exports use the original beast palette in each terrain; monster9..15 and player6..8 can vary in other fights.
No complete world traversal, gameplay modification, public verification or new HD art is claimed.
